title: CompletableFuture vs Future — blocking vs non-blocking, chaining, composition

s1_definition.profdef: `Future<V>` (Java 5) is a handle to a pending result — but it's LIMITED: `get()` BLOCKS until done (no non-blocking way to get result), no chaining (can't say "when done, do X"), no composition (can't combine two Futures), no exception handling callbacks, and no manual completion. `CompletableFuture<V>` (Java 8) fixes ALL of these: non-blocking callbacks (`thenApply`, `thenAccept`), chaining (`thenCompose`), composition (`thenCombine`, `allOf`, `anyOf`), exception handling (`exceptionally`, `handle`), manual completion (`complete()`, `completeExceptionally()`), and async variants (`thenApplyAsync`). CompletableFuture IS a Future (implements it) plus much more.
s1_definition.analogy: **Future** = you submit a form and get a TOKEN NUMBER. All you can do: wait at the counter until they call your number (`.get()` — blocking). Can't say "when it's ready, call me" — you MUST stand there waiting. **CompletableFuture** = you submit a form and get a SMART PAGER. The pager vibrates when ready (non-blocking callback). You can chain: "when ready, calculate tax (thenApply), then send receipt (thenAccept)." You can combine: "when BOTH balance and score ready, decide loan." You don't have to stand at the counter.
s1_definition.oneliner: Future = blocking get() only. CompletableFuture = non-blocking callbacks + chaining + composition + exception handling + manual completion. CF is Future on steroids.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `Future<V>` (Java 5) is a handle to a pending result — but it's LIMITED: `get()` BLOCKS until done (no non-blocking way to get result), no chaining (can't say "when done, do X"), no composition (can't combine two Futures), no exception handling callbacks, and no manual completion. `CompletableFuture<V>` (Java 8) fixes ALL of these: non-blocking callbacks (`thenApply`, `thenAccept`), chaining (`thenCompose`), composition (`thenCombine`, `allOf`, `anyOf`), exception handling (`exceptionally`, `handle`), manual completion (`complete()`, `completeExceptionally()`), and async variants (`thenApplyAsync`). CompletableFuture IS a Future (implements it) plus much more.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** **Future** = you submit a form and get a TOKEN NUMBER. All you can do: wait at the counter until they call your number (`.get()` — blocking). Can't say "when it's ready, call me" — you MUST stand there waiting. **CompletableFuture** = you submit a form and get a SMART PAGER. The pager vibrates when ready (non-blocking callback). You can chain: "when ready, calculate tax (thenApply), then send receipt (thenAccept)." You can combine: "when BOTH balance and score ready, decide loan." You don't have to stand at the counter.

**One line to remember:** Future = blocking get() only. CompletableFuture = non-blocking callbacks + chaining + composition + exception handling + manual completion. CF is Future on steroids.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The legacy settlement service used Future** for async processing. To check settlement status: polling loop `while (!future.isDone()) sleep(100)` → wasted CPU + delayed response. To combine balance + credit score: `.get()` on first, `.get()` on second → sequential! To handle errors: try-catch around `.get()` → ugly, no recovery pipeline. Fix: migrated to CompletableFuture — non-blocking callbacks, parallel composition with `thenCombine`, error recovery with `exceptionally`. Code: 60% shorter. Latency: 40% lower (parallel). CPU waste: zero (no polling loops).

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 (Future).** `pool.submit(task)` → Future. `future.get()` → BLOCKS caller. No way to say "when done, do X." Must wait or poll.

**Step 2 (CF).** `supplyAsync(task)` → CF. `.thenApply(transform)` → registers callback. Caller continues. When task completes → callback fires automatically on completing thread. Non-blocking!

**Step 3 (Future combining).** Two Futures: must `f1.get()` then `f2.get()` — caller blocked for both. Even if submitted in parallel, the CALLER is still blocked.

**Step 4 (CF combining).** `thenCombine(otherCF, fn)` — both run in parallel, callback fires when BOTH done. Caller not blocked until `.join()`.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ FUTURE (Java 5) — limited ═══

  submit(task) → Future
  Future.get() → BLOCK! ███████████████ → result
  Future.isDone() → poll loop (CPU waste!)
  No chaining. No combining. No error callbacks.

  ═══ COMPLETABLEFUTURE (Java 8) — everything! ═══

  supplyAsync(task) → CF
  .thenApply(fn)     → callback (non-blocking!)
  .thenCombine(cf2)  → parallel merge
  .exceptionally(fn) → error recovery
  .join()            → collect when YOU choose

  Caller: ───submit───do other work──────collect───
  Task:   ───────────executing──────done→callback→
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Migration from Future to CF ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Settlement Service                               │
  │                                                    │
  │  BEFORE (Future):                                 │
  │  Future<Result> f = pool.submit(settle);          │
  │  while (!f.isDone()) sleep(100); // CPU waste!    │
  │  Result r = f.get(); // blocking!                 │
  │                                                    │
  │  AFTER (CompletableFuture):                       │
  │  CF.supplyAsync(settle)                           │
  │    .thenApply(confirm)       // non-blocking!     │
  │    .thenCombine(fetchTax, merge)  // parallel!    │
  │    .exceptionally(fallback)  // error recovery!   │
  │    .whenComplete(log);       // observe!          │
  │  60% less code. 40% lower latency. Zero polling.  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Future vs CompletableFuture API ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │  <<interface>> Future<V>      │
  │  + get(): V (BLOCKS!)        │
  │  + get(timeout): V           │
  │  + isDone(): boolean         │
  │  + cancel(boolean): boolean  │
  │  + isCancelled(): boolean    │
  │  NO callbacks!               │
  │  NO chaining!                │
  │  NO composition!             │
  └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                 │ implements
  ┌──────────────▼───────────────┐
  │  CompletableFuture<V>         │
  │  ALL of Future's methods PLUS:│
  │  + thenApply(fn): CF<U>      │  chain transform
  │  + thenCompose(fn): CF<U>    │  chain async
  │  + thenCombine(cf,fn): CF<V> │  parallel merge
  │  + allOf(cf...): CF<Void>    │  wait for all
  │  + anyOf(cf...): CF<Object>  │  first wins
  │  + exceptionally(fn): CF<T>  │  error recovery
  │  + handle(fn): CF<U>         │  both cases
  │  + complete(V): boolean      │  manual completion
  │  + supplyAsync(): CF<T>      │  async creation
  └──────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Future (Java 5) provides only blocking `get()`, polling `isDone()`, and cancellation. No callbacks, no chaining, no composition, no error handling pipelines. CompletableFuture (Java 8) is a complete async programming model: non-blocking callbacks (`thenApply`/`thenAccept`), async chaining (`thenCompose`), parallel composition (`thenCombine`/`allOf`/`anyOf`), error recovery (`exceptionally`/`handle`), and manual completion (`complete()`/`completeExceptionally()`).

The biggest difference: Future forces the caller to BLOCK or POLL. CompletableFuture lets you register callbacks that fire automatically when the result is ready — the caller is free to do other work. In banking: migrating from Future's polling loop (`while (!isDone()) sleep(100)`) to CF's callback chain → 60% less code, 40% lower latency (parallel composition instead of sequential get()), zero CPU wasted on polling.
